problem: The output noise variance is written as σ² = (N₀/2)∫₀ᵀ h²(τ)dτ. For a general filter the integral must run over every τ where h(τ) is nonzero; a filter impulse response longer than T would give more output noise than this formula predicts. The 0-to-T limits are valid only because the matched filter is confined to the pulse interval.
fix: Write σ² = (N₀/2)∫ h²(τ)dτ, and add: for the matched filter h(τ) = s(T − τ) is zero outside 0 ≤ τ ≤ T, so the integral reduces to ∫₀ᵀ h²(τ)dτ.

problem: "The filter folds the pulse about T" is loose and can mislead. With h(t) = s(T − t) the reflection is about t = T/2; what the sentence describes is a time reversal followed by a delay of T.
fix: Say: "The filter time-reverses the pulse and delays it by T, so the mirror image sits with its peak at t = T; every part of the pulse adds in phase at the sampling instant."

problem: The unit check "V²·s = W·s = J" is true only when the voltage is taken across a 1 Ω reference. Strictly V²·s = W·Ω·s, so the jump to joules is not dimensionally clean as written.
fix: State the normalisation: "with s(t) treated as a voltage across 1 Ω, V²·s ≡ W·s = J" (or treat s(t) as a normalised signal with unit-energy-per-second dimensions), then quote E = 1 mJ.
